reaction.episode: DIGESTION episode through October 23 (data not stale): SPX 7,623.68, -2.82% off its 120-day high, -0.99% below its 50-day but +4.56% above its 200-day; SMH 527.20 between zones (-21.53% off high, -8.33% vs 50-day), NVDA 210.96 above Zone 1; VIX 19.45 at its 5-day high with no rollover and HY OAS 3.23 calm; mechanical capitulation tally 1 of 4 (only credit-calm confirmed).
reaction.invalidation: A held SPX close above 7,820 with SMH above 600 and VIX rolling over would void the Watch stance — the digestion would be over, not deepening — and the trap ladder with it. Conversely, HY OAS above 4% voids the Watch stance from the other side: it stops being a digestion and becomes a regime break.

ladder.response: Arm Tranche A (25% of new money) as a staged probe per the deployment ladder — not a full position.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes in Zone 2 ($470–505) or NVDA closes in Zone 2 ($175–185) AND mechanical tally reaches 3 of 6

ladder.response: Hold Tranche A; do not chase the first print — wait for a second low that holds with the 10-year falling before adding.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $470 or NVDA closes below $175

ladder.response: No chasing the bounce; treat as a failed-retest confirmation. Entries only after the second low holds or the zone is reclaimed on a held close.
ladder.trigger: Bounce into SMH $580–600 or SPX 7,750–7,820, then a close back below the zone (the trap case)

ladder.response: Stand down: no new entries of any kind until credit and vol come back inside the bands.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS above 4% or VIX above 25

ladder.response: Digestion ends: disarm the trap ladder, resume the normal posture, and treat the Tranche C confirmation path (held close above the failure zone) as live.
ladder.trigger: Held SPX close above 7,820 with SMH above $600

reaction.trapRisk: With SMH between zones, NVDA above Zone 1, and zero capitulation signals confirmed, the first bounce is the most dangerous entry in this episode: it runs straight into the SMH $580–600 / SPX 7,750–7,820 failure zone that already rejected the tape once. Entries must wait for the retest verdict — a held close above the zone means resumption, a rejection means the failed-retest path — and any probe before that verdict stays small and defined-risk.

strategyPosture: Watch. This is a DIGESTION episode with no capitulation confirmed (tally 1 of 4) and the week's decisive prints — the October 28 FOMC decision and mega-cap earnings — still ahead, so the portfolio holds fire and lets the levels, not the headlines, call the next move.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking, but it is not yet a rollover: credit conditions can flip, and a rotation that keeps widening without a credit event still grinds the index sideways. Position for rotation — own the rotated-to strength (MA +10.05% over 1m, VST +2.52%) — not for a crash that credit has not confirmed.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average -13.99% from their 52-week highs versus SPY only -2.8% off its high, an 11.19-point divergence gap; the weakest Mag7 name, TSLA, sits -25.4% off its high while AAPL is just -1.1% off. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.23 and calm, so credit is not confirming a broad rollover.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The market story is that leadership is rotating out of the mega-cap complex while the broad index holds — a healthy changing of the guard, not a top.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS moving toward 40% or HY OAS breaking above 4% would flip this from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: Price is well behind fundamentals here, which is the opportunity shape — but a washout with no capitulation signal confirmed (tally 1 of 4) is not yet a bottom. The gap says buy the names eventually; the tape says not on the first bounce. MU is the exception to the patience rule in the other direction: at $877.55 it sits above the $845–860 probe shelf, so the probe window has already passed without a fill.
themes.dataAnchor: The washout is deep and broad: SMH is -21.53% off its 120-day high and -13.08% over 20 days; VRT is -48.9% off its high, LRCX -47.5%, AMAT -49.0%, ONTO -48.6%, AVGO -35.0%, with 33 dislocations flagged, most SENTIMENT_DRIVEN. But the fundamentals have not broken with the prices: AVGO revenue is growing 55% YoY with a 42.1% FCF margin, ONTO +22.1%, VRT +27.7%, LRCX +131.3%, AMAT +11.4% with a 20.1% FCF margin. Top conviction scores run AVGO 84 (tier A), ONTO 81, VRT 80 — yet conviction promotions are empty, so nothing has cleared the board's bar yet.
themes.label: AI infrastructure washout, fundamentals intact
themes.narrative: The market story is that the AI buildout trade is broken — semis, power, and AI suppliers have been sold hard for a month.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing into Zone 2 ($470–505) or NVDA into Zone 2 ($175–185) with the capitulation tally reaching 3 of 6.

themes.counterRead: Rates explain the multiple compression (AMAT's decline is flagged MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION, not fundamental decay) but they do not explain a credit event that has not happened. The risk is not today's level — it is a level that forces a credit response, which is why HY OAS, not the 10-year alone, is the stand-down gauge. Honesty flag: this run's FRED feed came in PARTIAL, so rate prints are last-good cache where the feed failed, not fresh prints.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year sits at 4.99% with a 2.64% real yield, the 2-year at 4.77%, the 30-year at 5.32%, and the 2s10s curve barely positive at +0.22 — restrictive in real terms, but not blowing out. The Fed funds rate (DFF) is 3.88% and the 10-year breakeven is 2.35%, so inflation expectations are contained. HY OAS at 3.23 confirms credit is not cracking alongside rates.
themes.label: Rates restrictive, not cracking
themes.narrative: The market story is that rates are the binding constraint on the AI trade — expensive money choking a leveraged buildout.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or the 10-year sustaining above ~5.5% would break this read.

themes.counterRead: Wait-and-see is the honest read, not a cop-out: with the decision two days out, the tape has priced anticipation (VIX up, index flat) without pricing an outcome. Any position taken Monday morning is a bet on Wednesday's print, not on the data in hand — so the posture stays Watch until the print forces a verdict.
themes.dataAnchor: The FOMC event carries HIGH signal strength with 12 headline hits, and the active-event list pairs it with the October 14 CPI event still active at HIGH strength. The tape already reflects the wait: SPY was flat on the day (-0.1%) and -0.52% over the month, QQQ +0.73% on the day but -4.25% over the month, and VIX sits at 19.45 — its 5-day high and +30.8% over 20 days — elevated but with no rollover signal confirmed.
themes.label: FOMC and mega-cap earnings gauntlet
themes.narrative: The market story this week is wait-and-see: everything hinges on the October 27–28 FOMC decision and the mega-cap earnings prints landing alongside it.
themes.watchFor: The October 28 FOMC decision and the accompanying mega-cap earnings prints, read against the SPX 7,750–7,820 failure zone.

themes.counterRead: The contagion narrative runs ahead of the evidence: these are the names that always fall hardest in a digestion, and their falls have not transmitted to credit or to the index. Treat them as a sentiment gauge, not a systemic signal — until HY OAS or lending standards say otherwise. BMNR (-21.76% 1m) is a holding, so this theme is lived, not theoretical, for this portfolio.
themes.dataAnchor: The damage is real but concentrated: CONL is -36.23% over the month (-8.52% on the day), SMR -36.37%, ASTS -34.49%, OKLO -30.61%, RKLB -28.16%, BMNR -21.76%, COIN -18.74%, ETH-USD -13.96% — against SPY -0.52% over the month and IWM -1.8%. The broad tape has not followed these names down, and HY OAS at 3.23 with loose lending standards says credit has not caught the fear.
themes.label: Leveraged-beta unwind stays contained
themes.narrative: The market story is that the damage in crypto-adjacent and leveraged beta names signals contagion spreading into the broader market.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or SPY accelerating below its 200-day (7,291.31) would turn a contained unwind into a systemic one.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move materializes around Wednesday's FOMC decision and earnings prints: either a capitulation push into SMH Zone 2 ($470–505) or NVDA Zone 2 ($175–185) that arms the first deployment tranche, or a bounce into the SMH $580–600 / SPX 7,750–7,820 failure zone whose retest verdict decides whether this digestion resumes upward or fails again.
